text:
Marathon Petroleum stock climbed 3.4% today after tumbling 8.6% over the past two weeks, recouping some losses as oil prices steadied and refinery operations remained robust. The bounce follows a period of sharp decline driven by falling crude prices — Brent dipped below $90 a barrel on hopes for Iran de-escalation — but today's rebound suggests the market is reassessing those peace prospects after mixed signals from U.S. officials about whether a real diplomatic deal is actually possible. With refineries running at 94.5% capacity and U.S. crude back above $99 a barrel, the immediate operating environment for a major refiner remains solid.

The broader picture is one of heightened uncertainty around Middle East tensions. While initial headlines about ending the Iran conflict sent oil prices lower (which hurts refiner margins), more recent statements from officials like Secretary of State Rubio casting doubt on negotiations may be steadying the outlook — suggesting investors see less downside risk to energy prices than they feared a few days ago.
